protocol.primary_metric: terminal progress on a 0-100 scale; victories reported separately
protocol.goal_rule: first completed initialization/iteration with mean development progress >=40; no success assigned to censored runs
protocol.checkpoint_selection: highest mean development progress, later iteration breaks ties
protocol.teacher_budget: same 16 paired source/target games and four resampled hidden-order scenarios per candidate in both effect arms; all simulation costs counted separately
protocol.training_seeds: paired within repeat and distinct between repeats; teacher seeds disjoint from PPO and final
protocol.final_policy_rule: protocol fixed before any final seeds; do not select checkpoint, recipe or treasure by final results
protocol.cost_scope: post-change preparation, teacher, PPO and development evaluation; source pretraining is recorded separately as a sunk cost
protocol.manual_preparation: one shared implementation and protocol preparation; no run-specific hand labels or treasure ID overrides
limits: fixed finite budget; failure to reach the target is right censored, not an exact speedup factor
three independent training seeds; held-out uncertainty does not replace between-training variation
matched random seeds do not imply identical state trajectories after actions diverge

numeric.conclusion: Report goal attainment and finite-budget progress; scratch censoring precludes an exact time-to-goal ratio.

effect.conclusion: Report goal attainment and finite-budget progress; scratch censoring precludes an exact time-to-goal ratio.

limits: One fixed PPO recipe and 64 direct rollout games per run; scratch results are budget censored.
Past source PPO is a separate sunk cost; its historical BC/teacher cost is unavailable, so no end-to-end training-cost claim is made.
Teacher simulation and semantic decisions are included; its scenario rollouts are distinct from complete actual games.
Three independent training repeats cannot establish a general algorithmic speedup.
Natural-play later treasure opportunities depend on previous policy actions; first-selection diagnostics are also reported.
Treasure option probabilities are conditional on the SelectTreasure family; actual picks given an offer are reported separately.
The selected checkpoint maximizes development progress, never treasure suppression.
Inference timing includes normal operating-system scheduling under the reported thread count; process peak memory is not an isolated model allocation.

shared_accounting_overhead.note: baseline conversion and accounting passes are shared study preparation, outside per-arm learning budgets

development_prototypes.reason: shared candidate projection allowed treasure preparation to alter unrelated action families; replaced by isolated treasure projection before final
